authoredPrompt: This figure is a three-dimensional coordinate plot showing two vectors in standard position together with both of their cross products. The axes are thin black lines carrying evenly spaced tick marks: a vertical one labeled z, one descending to the lower right labeled y, and one descending to the lower left labeled x. Two short orange arrows leave the origin, one pointing to the right and labeled u = <0, 2, 1>, the other pointing down and to the left and labeled v = <3, -1, 0>. A long red arrow runs from the origin downward and to the right, reaching the bottom of the frame, labeled u x v = <1, 3, -6>. A long teal arrow runs from the origin upward and slightly to the left, reaching the top of the frame, labeled v x u = <-1, -3, 6>. Each long arrow is wrapped in a dashed blue rectangular box whose edges project its tip back onto the coordinate directions, making the endpoint coordinates readable. Drawing both products from a common origin makes it plain that they lie along a single line but point in opposite senses, each standing perpendicular to the plane spanned by u and v. The plot supports the relation u x v = -(v x u).
authoredInteractions:
- Toggle between u x v and v x u: the learner switches the product order, the active cross-product arrow flips to the opposite direction along the same line and its coordinates change sign, making anti-commutativity visible.
- Button for stepping through the right-hand rule: the learner advances from aligning fingers with u, curling toward v, and extending the thumb, and the red result arrow appears at the final step, connecting the rule to the direction of u x v.
authoredContext:
We see that, in this case, u×v=−(v×u) (the figure). We prove this in general later in this section.

The cross products u×v and v×u are both orthogonal to u and v, but in opposite directions.

This figure is the 3-dimensional coordinate system. It has two vectors in standard position. The first vector is labeled “u = <0, 2, 1>.” The second vector is labeled “v = <3, -1, 0>.” It also has two vectors that are cross products. The first is “u x v = <1, 3, -6>.” The second is “v x u = <-1, -3, 6>.”
sourceQmd: OpenStax Calculus, chapter 12: Vectors in Space

discrepancies: The inactive v × u vector, upper dashed box, and top label are faded by default, whereas the source shows both cross-product vectors and both projection boxes prominently.
The dashed projection boxes are much lighter and less visually dominant than the dark blue dashed boxes in the source.
The generated figure occupies a much smaller central area with large empty whitespace, while the source figure fills the frame vertically.

evaluation.notes: The generated figure correctly represents the vectors, axes, cross products, and guide boxes, but the default fading and small scale reduce resemblance to the source.
